arm-A.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-A.summary: Morpheus confirms Trinity's hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake. She runs the building's exterior to the street — hall, fire escape, roof, across the rooftops, and down through a window into a back stairwell — while the Agents pursue and match her. She reaches a ringing booth on the street and is gone before a garbage truck crushes it, so the Agents are left with wreckage and no body, but with the crew's next target named as Neo.
arm-A.action: After Morpheus confirms the hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake, Trinity bursts into the hall into Agent Brown and his police unit and flees she plummets through the shattered glass and onto the fire escape. Finding Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, she climbs to the roof and runs the rooftops, clearing a 40-foot gap the cops cannot follow while Agent Brown duplicates the leap with the same unnatural grace. She launches from the roof's edge toward a lit window, dives, crashes through glass into a back stairwell, and — finding only wind where she expects Brown — gets to her feet despite her injuries. On the street she races a U-turning garbage truck to a ringing phone booth, answers it, and is gone before the truck pulverizes the booth; the Agents inspect the wreckage with no body, but leave with the next target named as Neo.

arm-B.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-B.summary: Trinity abandons her compromised hardline at the Heart O The City Hotel and runs Morpheus's improvised route to the phone at Wells and Lake. She re-centers on his order, is driven along a worsening path — hall, fire escape, rooftops, window, back stairwell, street — as each exit is closed or guarded in turn: the hall by Agent Brown, the alley below by Agent Smith. She clears a 40-foot gap that Brown then duplicates exactly, dives through a window, and crashes down a stairwell bleeding and broken, moving on adrenaline and discipline until she reaches a phone booth and answers it a split-second before a garbage truck destroys it. She gets out. The Agents are left with no pursuer to catch, but the informant's tip has given them the crew's next target, Neo, and a machine search is already running.
arm-B.action: The event is a single escalating chase that converts a contained victory over the police into a desperate improvisation, and ends by trading Trinity's narrow survival for a colder defeat: the betrayal hands the Agents their next target, Neo. The pivot is physical — the impossible leap — because it is the moment the world's rules are shown breakable by both the hunted and the hunters, and what lets Trinity cross a gap ordinary physics and the cops cannot. The whole run matters because she, not the machine, reaches the phone first, which preserves the crew's lead even as the search turns toward Neo.

state_triples.reading: Trinity is a soldier who manages fear as a discipline rather than feeling free of it: every beat of the run is a decision not to let fear touch her hands or her stride. She obeys Morpheus not out of blind trust but because she has no luxury left, and the calm she shows over the gap is the same re-collecting she does on the phone in the hotel — a trained refusal to spend hesitation she cannot afford. What she cannot manage is what she cannot see: her escape is real, but her belief that beating the physical chase is the whole fight is wrong

arm-A.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-A.summary: Morpheus confirms Trinity's hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake. She runs the building's exterior to the street — hall, fire escape, roof, across the rooftops, and down through a window into a back stairwell — while the Agents pursue and match her. She reaches a ringing booth on the street and is gone before a garbage truck crushes it, so the Agents are left with wreckage and no body, but with the crew's next target named as Neo.
arm-A.action: After Morpheus confirms the hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake, Trinity bursts into the hall into Agent Brown and his police unit and flees she plummets through the shattered glass and onto the fire escape. Finding Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, she climbs to the roof and runs the rooftops, clearing a 40-foot gap the cops cannot follow while Agent Brown duplicates the leap with the same unnatural grace. She launches from the roof's edge toward a lit window, dives, crashes through glass into a back stairwell, and — finding only wind where she expects Brown — gets to her feet despite her injuries. On the street she races a U-turning garbage truck to a ringing phone booth, answers it, and is gone before the truck pulverizes the booth; the Agents inspect the wreckage with no body, but leave with the next target named as Neo.

arm-B.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-B.summary: Trinity abandons her compromised hardline at the Heart O The City Hotel and runs Morpheus's improvised route to the phone at Wells and Lake. She re-centers on his order, is driven along a worsening path — hall, fire escape, rooftops, window, back stairwell, street — as each exit is closed or guarded in turn: the hall by Agent Brown, the alley below by Agent Smith. She clears a 40-foot gap that Brown then duplicates exactly, dives through a window, and crashes down a stairwell bleeding and broken, moving on adrenaline and discipline until she reaches a phone booth and answers it a split-second before a garbage truck destroys it. She gets out. The Agents are left with no pursuer to catch, but the informant's tip has given them the crew's next target, Neo, and a machine search is already running.
arm-B.action: The event is a single escalating chase that converts a contained victory over the police into a desperate improvisation, and ends by trading Trinity's narrow survival for a colder defeat: the betrayal hands the Agents their next target, Neo. The pivot is physical — the impossible leap — because it is the moment the world's rules are shown breakable by both the hunted and the hunters, and what lets Trinity cross a gap ordinary physics and the cops cannot. The whole run matters because she, not the machine, reaches the phone first, which preserves the crew's lead even as the search turns toward Neo.

arm-A.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-A.summary: Alone in his apartment, Neo is contacted through his own PC by an unseen party who types back, names him, and tells him to follow the white rabbit; a real knock answers the last message, and a drug deal with Choi is interrupted by Dujour's invitation. When he spots a white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket, he agrees to go. At a crowded, smoke-filled gathering of people dressed in black, Trinity approaches him by name, confirms she was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, presses her body to his, and whispers that the answer to his question is out there and will find him, then withdraws.
arm-A.action: Neo is at his PC when the screen blanks and a prompt appears reading 'Wake up, Neo.' He tries to type but the keyboard types a message on its own instead, ending with 'Knock, knock, Neo,' at which someone actually knocks and the screen goes blank. Still unnerved, he opens the door with the chain on to admit Choi and several friends two hours late, retrieves a disk hidden inside a hollowed-out copy of Baudrillard's Simulacra and Simulations, takes Choi's 'two grand,' and hands the disk through the crack. After Choi jokes that he needs to 'unplug,' Dujour urges him out; he refuses on account of work until he notices a small white rabbit pin among the dozens on her black leather jacket, at which he agrees to go. At a crowded, smoke-filled apartment full of people dressed in black, Neo stands alone with a bottle of beer, feeling out of place, when Trinity walks straight up to him, greets him by name, identifies herself as 'the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. database,' and refuses to move to a quieter spot because she has little time. She confirms she was on his computer, warns him he is in danger and being watched, presses her body to his, leans to whisper directly into his ear, and tells him the answer to his question is out there and will find him, though it cannot be explained, before melting back into the wall of bodies.

arm-B.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-B.summary: Alone in his apartment one night, Neo is contacted through his own PC by an unseen party that types messages the machine should not produce, ending with 'Follow the white rabbit' — and, on cue, a real knock answers the screen. He runs a disk-for-cash deal with Choi and Dujour as usual, but after the visitors leave he can no longer trust whether he is awake or dreaming. Dujour's small white rabbit pin then pulls him out against his better judgment, and at a crowded apartment gathering Trinity — a woman who names herself as the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. database — tells him she was on his computer, warns that he is being watched and in danger, and refuses to give him the answer because it has to be seen to be believed; when Neo asks 'What is the Matrix?' she says the answer is out there and will find him, then withdraws and leaves him standing amid the crowd as a sound closes over him.
arm-B.action: The screen at Neo's PC blanks and types its own messages — 'Wake up, Neo,' 'The Matrix has you,' 'Follow the white rabbit,' 'Knock, knock, Neo' — and a real knock meets the last one. Still unnerved, Neo keeps the chain on, retrieves a disk from a hollowed Baudrillard, takes Choi's 'two grand,' and completes the sale. After Choi jokes the night is mescaline and that he needs to 'unplug,' Neo is hit by a returning 'feeling of unrealness' and asks whether Choi has ever been unsure he was awake. He refuses Dujour's invitation because he has work tomorrow, until he spots a small white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which 'the room tilts' and he agrees to go. At the gathering, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as 'the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. D-Base,' confirms she was on his computer, warns that he is 'in danger' and 'being watched,' and, pressing close in the deafening industrial music, tells him he is 'looking for an answer' that must be seen to be believed; Neo voices 'What is the Matrix?' and she says the answer is 'out there,' that it will find him, then melts into the shifting wall of bodies as a sound presses in on him.

arm-A.title: Neo's ordinary life reasserts itself
arm-A.summary: The alarm drags Neo awake at 9:15 A.M. in his apartment, already late. His return from the gathering and his journey to work are elided: the event opens with him already in bed, then seated and still at his desk in the downtown Meta CorTechs office, watching the window cleaners instead of Rhineheart. Rhineheart lectures him without looking up and forces an either/or ultimatum about punctuality and his job. Neo answers with crisp, unbothered compliance — outwardly deferential, inwardly elsewhere — as the extraordinary recedes and the ordinary reclaims him.

state_triples.reading: Neo lets the ordinary world reclaim him. Where the previous event left him wide open to something vast, here he answers a real demand with real consequences — lose his job — in the flattest possible way, because none of it reaches who he now knows himself to be. His eyes stay on the window cleaners while Rhineheart asserts authority, and his 'Perfectly clear' is less surrender than dismissal: he has already checked out of a hierarchy that cannot touch him. arm-B.summary: The alarm drags Neo awake at 9:15 A.M. in his apartment, jolting him into alarmed consciousness; the story then names the downtown office of Meta CorTechs and drops him into it at his desk, where Rhineheart lectures him for lateness and hands down an either/or ultimatum that Neo answers with crisp, deferential compliance. Across the run, the pull toward something vast is temporarily smothered by the machinery of the ordinary world, which reasserts its claim on his body, his location, and his standing as an employee.
arm-B.action: An alarm clock wakes Neo at 9:15 A.M., startling him into alarmed consciousness in his apartment; the story then establishes the downtown headquarters of Meta CorTechs, a software development firm, and places Neo inside it at his desk, where Rhineheart lectures him without looking up from his typing, accuses him of believing the rules don't apply to him, and delivers an ultimatum to be on time or find another job, to which Neo replies with crisp, deferential compliance.

state_triples.reading: Neo lets the ordinary world close over him: the alarm yanks him back into a body and a schedule, and the office reasserts its claim with a petty reprimand he meets with flat, practiced compliance. His mind stays elsewhere — on the window cleaners, on the pull Trinity named — so his 'Perfectly clear' reads as the least-engaged way to end a conversation that doesn't touch who he thinks he is. The irony is that this 'special' accusation is trivially wrong about him, and his dismissal of the authority is a luxury about to be revoked.

state_triples.reading: Rhineheart performs authority as background noise — lecturing while he keeps typing, treating Neo as administrative friction rather than a person. He wants to erase the impression that Neo thinks he's special, but he is diagnosing a man he has never actually seen: Neo's distance comes from the search Trinity named, not from the petty insubordination Rhineheart imagines. His irritation is real but shallow, and his either/or ultimatum mistakes a cosmic restlessness for a timekeeping problem.

state_triples.reading: The skyscraper exists only to be named — the anonymous exterior becomes Meta CorTechs, the ordinary-world institution that the story drops Neo back into. Its identification is the hinge that turns the pull toward the unknown into a return to the known, and it frames the office as the machine that will try to discipline him before that machine is exposed as hollow.
The alarm clock is the instrument of the ordinary world's reassertion: it drags Neo out of sleep and back into a schedule, reopening the day that the office will try to discipline.
The clock-face shows 9:15 A.M. and nothing more; it is the ordinary-world fact that startles Neo into the day and anchors the reprimand to come.

affects_outside.enables: It re-establishes Neo inside the ordinary world's hierarchy so that the reprimand can serve as the prelude to the Agents' arrival, his interrogation, and his physical modification — the workplace's reach is about to be shown as merely the outer layer of a far更
affects_outside.blocks_or_costs: It costs Neo the momentum of his commitment to go with Trinity's people; the ordinary world's claim temporarily smothers the pull toward the unknown and keeps him seated at a desk he is about to be dragged from.
affects_outside.off_screen_reactor: The Agents, watching him, have no presence here but are the reason his lateness and 'special' attitude matter; their surveillance is what will convert this petty workplace friction into a physical threat.

arm-B.turns_on: The ordinary world's reassertion of control over Neo — the alarm, the office, the ultimatum — which for a moment smothers the pull toward the unknown and frames his compliance as the least-engaged way to end a conversation that doesn't touch who he really is.
